significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish both a form-(iii) law—“substitution rate scales with how strongly the target language’s lexicon colexifies the two senses ... not with resource level”—and a form-(ii) causal decomposition in which a shared fine-sense representation is selectively discarded by an output-language “lexicalization gate.” This would fix predictions for untested concept-language pairs and distinguish representational loss from output-stage lexicalization, a consequential refinement of the shared-internal-representation picture implicated by Wendler et al., “Do Llamas Work in English?” (ACL 2024), using the independently measurable typological structure supplied by CLICS³ (Rzymski et al., Scientific Data 2020); it therefore establishes both a broad behavioral phenomenon and a weighty mechanism. The negative branch is also informative: failure of the colexification relation or causal separation would rule out this gate account and favor faithful paraphrasing, resource limitations, or absent fine-grained target-language knowledge, although a mixed failure across its several subclaims would be less decisive. Topic-substitution check: replacing the gate, colexification scaling law, and silent-substitution phenomenon with the generic multilingual-representation topic would remove the specific law and decomposition supporting this above-median score.

reach.justification: The named handles are the per-language “SILENT-SUBSTITUTION rate,” “CLICS colexification strength” as a predictor, and the causally manipulable “gate direction” that can “force paraphrase”; together they offer both an audit and an intervention rather than merely an explanation. The CLICS-based relation is ex ante because known target-language lexical structure can flag concept-language pairs before generation or deployment, while the substitution rate itself is post hoc and gate steering operates during generation. After model-specific re-extraction, the gate direction alone supplies mainly a procedure for looking, but the asserted colexification–substitution scaling relation predicts what should recur across multilingual models, languages, and concept classes; this can inform MT evaluators and practitioners who gate or ship multilingual systems. Topic-substitution check: the generic topic would provide none of these handles, lead time, or transferable predictor, so the reach score rests on claim-specific deliverables rather than multilingual modeling’s general importance.
